results.evidence_summary: Published BMV work reports distinct RNA-capsid contacts among morphologically similar virions, with RNA identity affecting particle stability, RNA release and infection timing; older stabilization work also identifies RNA-protein interactions as essential to virion integrity under relevant conditions.

Asymmetric reconstruction of BMV RNA shows that shell-equivalent virions contain functionally relevant RNA organization not captured by shell morphology alone. The RNA is largely disordered rather than a single unique asymmetric conformation, so the useful hidden variable is an ensemble/contact organization rather than a fixed portal-like structure.

Published BMV studies report hysteresis/partial irreversibility and at least two disassembly pathways with different interaction classes and intermediate behavior, showing that one shared shell state vocabulary is insufficient to encode all direction/context-dependent transitions.

The targeted BMV literature contains substantial asymmetry/debt evidence, so the mirror-compatible fallback was not selected for this system. The framework retains external reversible controls from C023.

score.interpretation: The framework predicted relevant missing-variable classes before targeted BMV search in this pass.
score.strict_limit: This is not evidence of human-level novelty because equivalent observations are established prior art, and latent pretraining knowledge cannot be excluded.
